  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez introduced the staff report, and introduced
  Lieutenant Fraijo, who elaborated on the report.

DISCUSSION HELD  Discussion was held relating to: 1) the Recreation Department’s
  responsibilities in cases of emergency; 2) the Recreation Center
  would be used as a shelter during emergencies; 3) the Red Cross
  would provide emergency supplies; 4) the Public Services Department
  would be responsible for gathering food and water, while the
  Recreation Department would take the lead in distributing said items;
  5) that all city stakeholders participated in the preparation of the plans,
  and relevant staff have received the necessary training, though
  additional training is required to further refine processes; 6) the plans
  have been certified by the state and county and satisfies all
  requirements for emergency responses; 7) city staff have the contact
  information for all stakeholders; and 8) that the IT Department would
  be responsible for ensuring communications during emergencies.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez presented the staff report. She added that the City
  Manager has met with the Finance Director to review the
  recommendations previously made by the Commission. They
  recommended that, since the proposed fees were so low, that the
  programs instead be offered at no cost to residents. She warned,
  however, that zero fees would likely boost participation to the point
  that the programs would fill very quickly, which may cause some
  interested individuals to be turned away if there is no room for
  additional participants.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo suggested that interested individuals be given turns to
  participate so that nobody is turned away, to which Director Rodriguez
  spoke on facility and staffing limitations.

  Chair Fraijo spoke in favor of approving the recommendation of
  zeroing fees for residents for certain recreational activities. She also
  requested that the Commission be informed if individuals are turned
  away from participating in said activities.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ Director Rodriguez stated that it is staff’s goal to not turn anybody
  away; however, it would be irresponsible to avoid mentioning the
  possibility to the Commission. She expressed her optimism that staff
  would solve any participation issues that may arise.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez asked whether the City allows for a volunteer
LOPEZ  program, to which Director Rodriguez indicated that she would check
  with Human Resources.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo asked whether the fees would be reviewed annually, to
  which Director Rodriguez advised that the Director of Finance has the
  goal of reviewing them yearly. If any fiduciary issues arise, staff would
  present a report to the Commission, which would then make a
  recommendation to the Council.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda spoke in favor of the zeroing of fees as shown in the
  staff report. She also complained that residents find it difficult to be
  hired for the Recreation Department.

MOTION  A motion was made by Commissioner Roman, seconded by Chair
  Fraijo, to approve eliminating fees for recreation programs, as shown
  in the staff report. The motion was unanimously approved.

RECREATION
MANAGER UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda provided an update on the following
MANAGER ZEPEDA  programs and activities:

  1) The Recreation Department has fully reopened.
  2) Aquatics has opened both day and night swimming.
  3) All outdoor classes and programs have been moved indoors.
  4) Participation in programs such as Volleyball, Aquafitness, and
  Parent and Me lessons have returned to pre-COVID numbers.
  5) Day Camp, which has been fully subsidized by the Irwindale
  Community Foundation, has 40 students enrolled.
  6) Just under 150 individuals participated in the Movies in the Park
  events.
  7) Music in the Park had a great turnout its 1st week.
  8) Beach trips are kicking off this month. However, despite the
  Irwindale Community Foundation having subsidized the program,
  the minimum number of participants was not reached and the first
  trip was cancelled.
  9) Registrations for the Family Camp Out event begins July 19.
  10) Aquatics programs, which include Day Swim, Night Swim, Senior
  Splash, and Aquabilities, have begun. Swimming lessons began
  this week with 66 participants. Parent and Me has 21 participants,
  not including their parents.
  11) She thanked all participants and volunteers for the success of the
  recent 4th of July Yard Decorating Contest.
  12) The Rocking Rec Drive Thru event was held July 3.
  13) Despite the lack of advertisement for the event, the 4th of July
  Fireworks Show was a great success with a park full of viewers.
  14) She also welcomed newly hired/promoted staff.

ROMAN  Manager Zepeda advised that the cleaning crew cleans the

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda asked about how children with split residencies in

  1) He thanked the maintenance workers for working on lighting

  2) Some labels have been received for the exercise equipment.
  These will be placed on the equipment.
  3) Everything worked smoothly during the 4th of July Fireworks
  Spectacular; no fireworks were reported and no damage to parks

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez asked about dry spots on the park lawn, to
LOPEZ  which Supervisor Rodriguez advised that some areas of the park will
  have the irrigation upgraded in a future phase of the Park
  Improvement Project. He also noted that an old water line at the east

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo noted large vermin causing damage at the park, to which
  Supervisor Rodriguez noted that staff is working on addressing the
  matter with the help of a pest management company.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda thanked the Senior Center Bus Driver for helping
  beautify the park by picking up litter.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE

DIRECTOR  Director of Public Services Rodriguez presented the following update:
RODRIGUEZ
  1) The City Council has approved the creation of a full-time Aquatics
  Supervisor and four part-time Aquatics staff. The Supervisor
  would be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the
  pool. Job descriptions will be mailed to residents tomorrow.
  2) Staff has worked on addressing the effects that the recent
  fireworks show had on the pool’s water chemistry.
  3) The City Council also approved the hiring of full-time Senior
  Recreation Leaders.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Replying to a question by Chair Fraijo, Director Rodriguez advised
  that the newly-formed Aquatics Department would present reports
  and information to the Commission. She added that the Bus Driver
  would also assist in the maintenance of the pool, and that the Aquatics
  Supervisor would oversee all pool programs.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda asked why whiffle ball activities were cancelled
  recently, to which Director Rodriguez indicated that several staff
  members called out from work that day and there was nobody
  available to teach the class. However, the activities resumed today.

SUZANNE GOMEZ  Responding to several questions by Suzanne Gomez, Director
  Rodriguez indicated that: 1) the Aquatics Supervisor position would
  be advertised externally, 2) the Irwindale Community Foundation has
  sponsored several Recreation classes and activities, and 3) there are
  no plans for the upcoming year for a renovation of the pool, though
  staff plans on adding pool renovations to the Capital Improvement
  Project list. Suzanne Gomez thanked all city departments for the
  phenomenal job they are all doing.

COMMISSIONER ITEMS
AND REQUESTS

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman requested that the wading pool be cleaned.
ROMAN

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Lopez thanked staff for their wonderful work and
LOPEZ  wished everyone a great summer.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman asked about hiring Summer Youth workers
ROMAN  next year, and requested a “nostalgic night” for Movies in the Park
  sessions.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  JULY 7, 2021
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 7

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo asked about requirements for wearing masks indoors, to
  which Director Rodriguez said she would consult with Human
  Resources. She noted, however, that members of the public may visit
  city facilities and that, if they are not vaccinated, they should wear
  masks. Furthermore, masks are required at youth settings such as
  the Recreation Building or the Library.

VICE CHAIR ZEPEDA  Vice Chair Zepeda thanked staff for the amazing 4th of July Fireworks
  Spectacular, and thanked the Police Department for having attended
  and the Public Works Department for helping clean the park.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo asked that an item be added to next month’s agenda to
  discuss use of water flotation or therapeutic devices inside the pool.
  She also requested that flyers be sent to residents informing them of
  how they can volunteer.

ADJOURNMENT  There being no further business to conduct, the meeting was
  adjourned at 7:40 p.m.

Recommendation:

Receive and file the Irwindale Recreation Usage Statistics for 2019-2021.

Administrative Action:

 Submitted/Approved by:

 Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director
 (626) 430-2211

Background and Analysis:

At the June 23, 2021 City Council Meeting , Mayor Pro Tern Burrola directed staff to
provide the Recreation Usage Statistics for 2019 for review and discussion. The request
specifically asked for the report to provide the number of residents and non-residents
attending each class, program and event provided by Irwindale Recreation.

The attached report was presented to the City Council at its July 28th meeting and
provides the usage statistics for calendar years 2019, 2020, and preliminary numbers for
2021 . The report identifies the number of resident and non-resident attendees for each
program, class, or event offered each year along with the total number of attendees. In
addition, the staffing levels are included, which identifies the number of Senior Recreation
Leaders and Recreation Aides required to offer the programs/events/classes.

For many of the events such as Movies in the Park, Music in the Park, 4th of July
Spectacular, Ml Fiesta, etc., there is only a total number of attendees listed. Staff uses a
hand tally counter to determine the number of people attending these events.

The numbers provided under Calendar Year 2020 reflects the new virtual programs and
drive by/through events provided as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Some of these
new events and virtual classes include Family Time Valentine, Reverse Trunk or Treat,

  Page 1
 Scarecrow Alley, Yard Decorating Contests, Tot Boxes, Tiny Tots Virtual Crafts, Virtual
Cheer and Munchkin Cheer, and a variety of virtual painting classes for all ages.

Staff also provided the preliminary numbers for calendar year 2021. These numbers
reflect the programs, classes, and events held from January to June 2021.

The attached report findings identified the percentage of resident attendance was higher
in 2019 and 2021 for special events that required registration and the programs offered
by Irwindale Recreation. Special Events requiring registration showed 91 % resident and
9% non-resident attendance in 2019 and 87% resident and 13% non-resident attendance
in 2021. Programs and activities identified 69% resident and 31 % non-resident
attendance in 2019 and to date, 70% resident and 30% non-resident attendance in 2021 .
Aquatics findings determined a higher usage among non-residents with 26% residents
and 74% non-residents in 2019 and 30% residents and 70% non-residents in 2021.

Background and Analysis :

At the July 7, 2021 Parks and Recreation Meeting , Chair Fraijo requested Staff send out
an informational flyer on how residents can volunteer at the Dan Diaz Recreation Center.
City Staff has prepared the attached flyer inviting potential volunteers to attend a meeting
at the Dan Diaz Recreation Center on August 26, 2021 at 6:30 pm. Staff is looking for
individuals 13 years and older to volunteer at its major events such as Easter
Eggstravaganza, 4th of July Spectacular, Ml Fiesta, Halloween Spooktacular, and
Christmas Spectacular. However, Staff was informed by CJPIA, the City's insurance
company, that it is their recommendation that only students 15 years or older be eligible
to volunteer due to insurance liability. Therefore, Staff will only be allowed to accept
students 13-14 year olds to volunteer if it is required for school service hours or the
students are members of Irwindale Teen Club.

The City of Irwindale has a more extensive Volunteer Program established through the
City's Human Resources/Risk Management Department that allows individuals to
volunteer on a long-term basis in City Departments, including the Dan Diaz Recreation
Center. At this time, the City of Irwindale is not accepting external volunteers of this caliber
due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 Issue:  Senior Splash

Recommendation:

Review and make recommendations to the current guidelines for all recreational swim
hours, which include Day and Night Swim , Senior Splash and Aquabilities.

Administrative Action:

 Submitted by:

 Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager
 (626) 430-2226

 Reviewed I Approved by:

 Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director

Background and Analysis:

Irwindale Aquatics provides a variety of healthy, affordable and safe programs and
services to the Irwindale community and its visitors. These include, but are not limited to,
Recreational Swim, Swimming Lessons, Aquafitness, and Lap Swim. In 2019, City
Council approved funding to allow for additional Aquatics programs and classes which
include Senior Splash, Aquabilities, and more. Senior Splash and Aquabilities are
recreational swim hours for targeted groups. Senior Splash serves our 50+ population
and Aquabilities serves are friends with special needs.

Recreational swim is an opportunity for patrons to swim and play in the pool at their
leisure. In an effort to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all patrons, there are
basic rules in place. These rules were designed for the safety of all participants and are
in line with community pool standards. These rules are posted at our facility and include:

  Page 1
  1.  Obey the lifeguard at all times.
 2.  Showering down is required when entering the pool.
 3.  Absolutely no running , horseplay or roughhousing in the lockers, showers, or deck
  areas of the pool.
 4. Food, gum, beverages and smoking are prohibited.
 5. Water diapers are allowed and required for children 3 and under.
 6. An adult must accompany children younger than 6 years old .
 7. Only persons in swimsuits are allowed on the deck area.
 8. Only regular designed swimsuits are allowed in pool. No cutoffs, g-strings, t-shirts
  or other makeshift swimsuits permitted.
 9. Persons with bandages, open sores, skin disease, fungus , etc. are not allowed in
  pool.
 10. No swimming aids, toys or personal water equipment allowed in pool with the
  exception of goggles.
 11 . Loitering in locker rooms is not allowed.
 12. No swimming in diving area.
 13. Non-swimmers must stay in shallow water.
 14. No radios, headphones, strollers or other personal gear allowed on deck area.
 15. Vandalism or property defacement is strictly prohibited.
 16. Management is not responsible for lost or stolen property.
 17. Be considerate of other swimmers.
 18. Only one person at a time on the diving board.
 19. No running back and forth on diving board.
 20. Children in wading pool must be 6yrs or younger and accompanied by an adult.
 21 . Regular diapers are not permitted.
 22. Only one person at a time on the diving board.
 23. All participants using the diving boards must be able to swim.
 24. No flotation devices or life vests allowed .
